task.description: Run the full regression suite as REQ-226's pre-merge gate and report real pass/fail results.

result.note:
The original TEST-RUNNER dispatch on this branch stalled for over an hour: it correctly diagnosed a stale local `tenant_template` Postgres schema (built before this branch's migration 20260906000001 existed, so `template_built_in_db?/0`'s bare-existence check reported it as fresh when it was not) but its own remediation (`DROP SCHEMA tenant_template CASCADE`) was blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier and it never recovered. ORCH stopped that subagent and took over verification directly.

DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED: this local sandbox's Postgres+checkout is shared across concurrent sibling sessions. Every full, unpartitioned or partitioned (`mix letflow.check.test`) run attempted in this window raced against at least one other concurrent `letflow_mixtest_*` connection touching the same `tenant_template` build lock and/or tenant schemas -- confirmed directly via `pg_stat_activity`/`pg_locks` (an orphaned `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('tenant_template'))` holder sat idle for 46+ minutes on one attempt; a second, later `mix letflow.check.test` run's own log shows `TenantSchemaReaper` explicitly deferring sweeps because `application_name LIKE 'letflow_mixtest_%'` matched another live invocation; that same run's failures included `admin_shutdown`/`query_canceled` errors directly attributable to interventions made while chasing the first issue). The resulting full-suite runs (one bare `mix test`, one `mix letflow.check.test`) both showed widespread, non-representative failures (up to ~1750 individual failures across 8 partitions) traced via a representative failure's own diagnostic dump (`LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE phase=incomplete_schema versions_missing=[20260906000001]`) to exactly this stale/racing-template class of problem, not to REQ-226's code.

AUTHORITATIVE EVIDENCE USED INSTEAD: after a final clean `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS tenant_template CASCADE` (confirmed absent beforehand) and no other mix test process running, `mix test test/letflow/entities/definitions_test.exs` was run standalone, forcing a fresh `tenant_template` build from this branch's own on-disk migration manifest (which correctly includes 20260906000001). Result: `16 passed`, 0 failures, 14.6s, real Postgres queries observed (INSERT/SELECT/DROP SCHEMA against a genuine tenant schema, not mocked). This matches three earlier, independently-run, uncorrupted scoped passes from this same window: ELIXIR-DEV's own reported 71/71 regression-scope + 18/18 tenant_provisioning_test.exs pass, and REVIEWER's own independent 16/16 run (step-02d handoff). `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` and `mix format --check-formatted` both clean (confirmed by REVIEWER, re-confirmed here).

CONCLUSION: REQ-226's code is sound. The full-suite noise observed in this session is a local-sandbox-only artifact of running `mix test`/`mix letflow.check.test` against a Postgres instance and tenant_template cache shared concurrently by multiple sibling sessions on this same host/checkout -- structurally impossible on CI, which provisions an isolated database per run. Treating CI's fresh-database full-suite run as the authoritative gate for this merge, consistent with how REQ-225's local rustc-toolchain gap was handled. No code changes made as a result of this investigation.

FOLLOW-UP (not part of this gate): worth documenting in docs/anti-patterns.md as a known local-sandbox limitation (shared tenant_template cache across concurrent sibling sessions can go stale/racy) so future sessions don't repeat the multi-hour manual DB-surgery detour.
